title: Lookalike Verbs: 切る or 着る?
description: Pairs that sound alike but conjugate differently — type the right form in context.

points.title: う-verbs that look like る-verbs
points.summary: Lookalike verbs: Verbs that sound the same (or almost) but belong to different types.
points.body:
- **切る** (cut) is an う-verb → 切って, 切らない — **着る** (wear) is a る-verb → 着て, 着ない.
- **帰る** (go home) → 帰って, 帰らない — **変える** (change) → 変えて, 変えない.
- **要る** (need) → 要らない — **いる** (be) → いない.
- **入る** (enter) → 入って — **入れる** (put in) → 入れて.
- **知る**, **走る**, **喋る**, **滑る**, **焦る**, **減る** look like る-verbs but are う-verbs.

Tip: learn each exception together with its ない-form (帰らない, 知らない) — that form gives the type away.
examples: {美容院|びよういん}で{髪|かみ}を{短|みじか}く切りました。
I had my hair cut short at the salon.
